title: Graceful degradation: fast-recovery surge absorber and soft-circuit hotfix
author: Aisha Khatri
description: Context: weekend traffic spike exposed a pathological interaction between hard circuit resets and the SLO enforcer that led to prolonged regional evictions. This PR implements a 'surge absorber' soft-circuit and a fast-recovery path to reduce time-to-recovery while bounding quality impact. Motivation: avoid long outage windows caused by repeated hard-circuit trips and quota thrash during bursts; maintain availability for small/low-cost requests without sacrificing operator control. Implementation summary: introduce a per-route transient token-budget bucket and a soft-circuit state machine (open -> absorbing -> degraded -> recovering), integrate with the SLO enforcer to mark degraded responses and emit explicit degradation_reason tags, add a fast-recovery router that routes compact responses to a low-latency fast-model replica when allowed, add feature flag gating (runtime.surge_absorber.v1) and canary rollout controls, and update dashboards/runbook. Backwards compatibility and ops: feature is opt-in; default off for Dedicated and Private deploys. Operators can configure per-tenant thresholds and disable fast-recovery routing. Checklist: [x] unit tests for state transitions and budget accounting; [x] integration tests with SLO enforcer; [x] perf-canary in benchmark-lab; [x] dashboards and alerts updated; [x] runbook and rollback steps documented; [x] Linear ticket(s) referenced (ENG-1823). Rollout plan: staged canary in eu-west-1 then us-west-2; automated gates on error-rate, degraded_response_rate, and embedding/regression signals; automatic rollback if quality regress > 3% on canary. Metrics added: runtime.surge_absorber.state, runtime.surge_absorber.recovery_time_ms, runtime.surge_absorber.degraded_response_rate. Notes: this is a targeted reliability improvement (not a model change). See ENG-3890 for follow-up harmonization across other soft-circuit implementations.

review_comments: Marco Jensen: Can we ensure the budget bucket is persisted across short process restarts? Response: we persist the bucket epoch to etcd; kept the retention tiny to avoid state bloat and added tests around restart semantics.

Priya Nair: Concern about double-counting tokens when fallback triggers; please add a guard. Response: added atomic accounting and a new unit test (surge_absorber_test.go::TestNoDoubleCount) and recorded the invariant in comments.

Ethan Cole: Please add observability to distinguish soft vs hard circuit evictions. Response: added runtime.surge_absorber.degraded_response_rate and emit evict_reason label (soft|hard) for existing eviction metrics.
Priya Nair (approval): Verified canary in eu-west-1 for 6h, metrics within thresholds. Approving to merge.
release_notes: Adds a gated ‘surge absorber’ soft-circuit to reduce full-region evictions during spikes and a fast-recovery routing path for low-cost responses. Opt-in via runtime.surge_absorber.v1. Includes metrics, dashboards, and an updated runbook.
testing_summary: Unit: 12 new tests, 40 updated. Integration: SLO enforcer integration tests passing. Perf-canary: benchmark-lab 20-minute 2x-load run showed 41% fewer full-region evictions and 18% lower mean recovery time. Canary: staged 6-hour run in eu-west-1 with automated gates; no quality regressions observed above thresholds. CI: all checks green.
notes: Hotfix intent: addresses a production incident 2026-01-17 where repeated hard-circuit resets caused cascading regional evictions. This change reduces blast radius and improves recovery time; follow-up work planned to generalize soft-circuit policy across other routing layers (ENG-3890).
